title.narrative: Tanzania Maternal and Child Health Investment Program

description.narrative: The objective of the Second Additional Financing (AF2) to the Maternal and Child Health Investment Program is to scale up the provision and improve the quality of essential health care services, with a focus on maternal and child health. The AF2 will support the parent Program through an expansion of its scope in the provision and access of essential health services. The AF2 will support results related to increasing capacity for training health workers, Disbursement-Linked Indicator (DLI), enhanced functionality of health facilities (DLIs 7 and 7.1), and building capacity management and accountability (DLI 8). The parent Program includes an ambitious scale-up of primary health care (PHC) facilities, and the AF2 further supports this scale-up to enhance the quality of primary health services, particularly for maternal and child health (MCH).
To scale up the provision and improve the quality of essential health care services, with a focus on maternal and child health.

condition.narrative: Section I.A.2 of the Schedule to the Project Agreement:MoH(Z) shall establish by not later than thirty (30) days after theEffective Date, and thereafter maintain throughout the period of Project implementation, a Project management team (“MoH(Z) PMT”):(a) headed by a Project Coordinator/Manager assisted by competent staff with experience and qualifications, in numbers and underterms of reference, acceptable to the Association; and (b) vested with such powers, financial resources, functions andcompetencies, acceptable to the Association, as shall be required for it to carry out the day-to-day implementation (management andcoordination) of Project activities.

Section I.B.1 of the Schedule to the Project Agreement:The RGoZ shall prepare and adopt by not later than thirty (30) days aftereffectiveness, a Project Operation Manual, in a manner and substance satisfactory to the Association, and shall thereafterimplement the Project in accordance therewith.

Section I.B.1(a) of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:GoT to establish, by not later than thirty (30) days aftereffectiveness, and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of the Operation, a Joint Steering Committee, headedby the Permanent/Principal Secretary of MoH, and co-chaired by the Permanent/Principal Secretaries of PO-RALG and MoH(Z), to beresponsible for the approval of the Program Operation Manual, the Program's annual budget, the Program Reports, the Annual WorkPlans and Budgets, and the endorsement of the DLIs/DLRs annual verification reports, as further detailed in the Program OperationManual.

Section I.B.1(b) of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:GoT to establish, by not later than thirty (30) days aftereffectiveness, and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of the Program, program management teams withinPO-RALG (“PO-RALG PMT”) and MoH (“MoH PMT”) respectively, which teams shall be: (a) lead by a Program Coordinator assisted bycompetent staff, with experience and qualifications, in numbers and under terms of reference, acceptable to the Association; and(b) vested with such powers, financial resources, functions and competencies, acceptable to the Association, as shall be requiredfor them to carry out the day-to-day implementation of Program activities.

Section I.C.1 of the Schedule to the Project Agreement:The RGoZ shall, by no later than April 30th of each year during theimplementation of the Project, prepare and furnish to the Association an annual work plan and budget containing all activitiesproposed to be carried out under the Project during the following Fiscal Year, including the annual training plans, as well as theproposed financing plan for the expenditures required thereunder, indicating the envisioned amounts and source of financing.

Section I.D.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:GoT appoint by not later than thirty (30) days after effectiveness, andthereafter maintain at all times during the implementation of the Program, an independent verification agent with experience andqualifications and under terms of reference acceptable to the Association, to: (a) verify the data and other evidence supportingthe achievement of the DLIs/DLRs; and (b) recommend the corresponding disbursements to be made, as applicable.
